change: History trimming. A checkpoint may now be a Loro shallow snapshot. After the final save, a session that edited a document over 4 MiB writes one more checkpoint (Store::close_job) keeping that session's history when the result fits 4 MiB, else none. While open, a checkpoint over 16 MiB trims the same way; compaction trims to the latest version. Rollback rebuilds trimmed documents from their starting state; versions before the start are stale_base; concurrent text edits branch from a state-only export instead of fork_at; a retention floor stops a stale text base from saving updates that depend on trimmed history.
why: document-growth-2026-10-01.json: Doodle Board filled the 32 MiB limit on day 18.87 (releaseBlocked) while its live value was 39 bytes; every checkpoint kept the full history.

storeCost.note: checkpointExportMS is now a maintenance checkpoint (full snapshot below 16 MiB); compactExportMS is slop compact (trim to the latest version). Baseline: rust-storage-2026-10-01.json layoutSplit.storeCost.after.

verification: bun run check && bun run test
bun run build && bun run swift:test (continuousEditingStillAutosaves failed intermittently under load; it passes alone and touches no changed path)

loroFindings.forkAtOnShallow: LoroDoc::fork_at returns NotImplemented("fork_at on shallow docs") in 1.16.2, which failed every concurrent text edit on a trimmed document.
loroFindings.unopenablePackage: An update whose dependencies precede a shallow checkpoint's start fails to import (ImportUpdatesThatDependsOnOutdatedVersion), so such a saved update would make the package unopenable; hence the retention floor.
loroFindings.deletedContentAtACut: A shallow snapshot at an earlier version keeps everything deleted before the cut in its starting state. Two sessions of 160 inserted-and-removed 32 KB rows: full history 14.5 MB; cut at the last session's start 15.8 MB (state-only export at the cut 5.3 MB with 2 live rows); cut at the latest version 639 bytes.
loroFindings.trimCost: A shallow export re-encodes what it keeps instead of reusing Loro's cached snapshot, and a cut at an earlier version first rebuilds the state there: 3500x1000 maintenance trimming to the previous checkpoint took 272 ms on the edit queue against 32 ms to the latest version. Hence trimming at close, not during maintenance.
loroFindings.partialImport: Loro applies the changes of a mixed blob that it can and refuses those depending on trimmed history; Document::import publishes what landed before returning stale_base.
loroFindings.branchCost: text_cost branch slow path p95: state-only branch 36-41 ms, fork_at 36-39 ms on the same machine.
